examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Choose BFS for unweighted graphs, topological relaxation for DAGs, Dijkstra for nonnegative weights and Bellman–Ford when negative weights may occur. Reachable negative cycles can destroy finite shortest-walk distances. Relaxing over a larger permitted edge count cannot increase its minimum.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A DAG has s→a:2,s→b:7,a→b:−3,b→t:4,a→t:8. What is shortest distance s→t?

**Answer: 3.** Topological relaxation gives d(a)=2,d(b)=min(7,2−3)=−1,d(t)=min(10,−1+4)=3. Path s→a→b→t achieves it.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Dijkstra's standard proof requires nonnegative weights. A minimum spanning tree and a shortest-path tree optimize different objectives.

Dijkstra is not generally correct in graphs with negative edges, even when no negative cycle exists.
